_comment: WC2026 QUARTER-FINAL (QF100: winner of Argentina-Egypt vs winner of Switzerland-Colombia) -- the last QF. KNOCKOUT: no draw -- level after 90' -> extra time -> penalties, so the deliverable is who ADVANCES. Winner meets the England-Norway winner in the semi-finals (M102). Routes: Argentina WON Group J with a PERFECT nine (rating 95) but has had TWO STRAIGHT knockout scares: 3-2 aet vs Cape Verde (a proven block dragged them to extra time) and 3-2 vs Egypt (2-0 DOWN until the 80th before three late goals). The ARGENTINA-SPECIFIC standing note applies: a RELIABLE advancement bet (86-90% priced, always through) but a BAD clean-sheet/controlled-win bet -- organized underdogs have scored TWO on them twice; their games run chaotic and high. Switzerland WON Group B (1-1 Qatar, 4-1 Bosnia, 2-1 Canada; rating 81), beat Algeria 2-0 in the R32 (clean sheet) and survived the R16 0-0 shootout vs Colombia. Organized, balanced, competent -- solid defence, modest attack, NO elite striker -- and now a proven shootout survivor. Class gap ~14 (95 vs 81) -> Argentina a heavy favourite. RULE TENSION resolved: the BTTS rule (clear favourite + no elite striker -> lean No) is MODULATED by the Argentina note (2 direct observations: goals up, clean sheet down) -> Switzerland kept at lambda 0.83 (mild trim only), BTTS near-neutral 50.4% (NOT forced to No), Argentina clean sheet 43.6% (not the 50%+ a naive read would give). Texture: Argentina should win with goals (2-0/2-1/3-1 cluster, Over lean 56.6%) but the Swiss-organized profile is exactly the type that has scored on them -- and if Switzerland drags it deep, they just won a shootout (ET 20.9%, pens 9.6% priced honestly). RECAL: first pass sat 2.7 pts below the market on Argentina (63.4 vs 66.1); applied don't-fade-the-elite, lifted ARG 2.00 -> 2.12 / trimmed SUI 0.85 -> 0.83 to align (66.4 vs 66.1, div 1.0). Home = Argentina (nominal; neutral venue). Cards not modelled (referee TBD).

_postmatch.result: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland AFTER EXTRA TIME (1-1 at 90'). Argentina advance to the semi-finals (where they meet England). Their THIRD straight knockout going deep/chaotic -- and their third straight 3-goal output.

_postmatch.verdict: Clean process hit, and the ARGENTINA-SPECIFIC note is now 3-for-3. Argentina advanced as the 79.8% pick (✅), but again NOT in regulation: 1-1 at 90' (1-1 was a top-3 scoreline at 9.9%), the ET branch (20.9%) fired, and Argentina's class told in the extra 30' -- 3-1. Every Argentina-specific texture read landed: (1) NO clean sheet again -- Switzerland (the organized-underdog profile that keeps scoring on them) nicked one, the THIRD straight knockout where Argentina concedes; keeping BTTS near-neutral (50.4%) instead of the rule's default lean-No was right. (2) GOALS UP again -- Argentina scored 3 for the third straight knockout (3-2, 3-2, 3-1); the Over lean (56.6%) landed. (3) The capped clean sheet (43.6%, not 50%+) was the honest number. And like England-Norway the same day-cycle, the layered forecast worked: a ~80% favourite with a 21% ET branch is EXPECTED to sometimes need extra time -- that is the priced path. Switzerland's 20.2% included exactly this: drag it level to 90', hope in the lottery -- they got to the door but Argentina finished it in ET, no shootout needed.
_postmatch.lesson: The team-profile layer of the calibration is now delivering consistent value: ARGENTINA (3 knockouts: 3-2 aet, 3-2, 3-1 aet) = reliable advancement (~80-90% priced, always through), always ~3 goals scored, always concedes, often deep -- price their games Over/BTTS-live/ET-fat and never price a controlled clean-sheet win. This is a stable, exploitable profile heading into the SEMI vs England, whose own profile (real attack, leaky defence, BTTS-Yes in 5 of 6, just went to ET too) points the SAME direction: the England-Argentina semi projects as an OPEN, high-scoring, both-score, potentially deep classic -- the two most chaotic profiles left, meeting. France-Spain projects as the opposite texture (the two best defences). The semi-final forecasts write themselves from the banked profiles; validate against the market as always.
